reasons: Missing-behaviour claim is supported: cited Section 9.3 and the surrounding cause-based termination scheme contain no Customer convenience right, while Section 2.1 confirms a three-year committed term (>12 months), which the rule's detection guidance treats as a deviation.

The inserted Section 9.4 tracks the rule's preferred position and model language closely (30 days' written notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, no early-termination fee) and confirms Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right during a term, consistent with the redline guidance.

The consequential edit to Section 2.1 is minimal and directionally correct for the customer: it deletes only the words waiving termination rights and adds a narrow proviso subordinating the take-or-pay commitment to Section 9, preventing the commitment from operating as a de facto early-termination penalty. Deterministic checks confirm both operations apply and the p0012 edit is minimal.
Section numbering (9.4) fits the existing gap between 9.3 and 9.5, so the insert is structurally coherent; no Vendor convenience right exists elsewhere, so no deletion was required.

Comment is concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position, explains the change, and offers the 60-day fallback without lecturing; severity high is appropriate for loss of exit rights under a USD 2,000,000/year multi-year commitment.
